title: Cyrus and the Confession
premise: Mirabel Kavanagh has spent twelve years chronicling the 1993 disappearance of schoolteacher Ada Wren in her podcast 'The Cold File,' but when twin letters arrive — one confessing to the crime, one promising a second confession at the town's thirtieth anniversary dinner — she realizes the case was never cold, only curated. As she investigates, Mirabel discovers the letters were sent by two different people: dying former sheriff's deputy Cyrus Bell, who covered up what he saw to protect his found family of misfit townsfolk, and Ada herself, alive and hiding in plain sight as the anniversary dinner's caterer. The climax erupts at the dinner, where Cyrus publicly confesses not to murder but to the town's collective silence, forcing Ada to choose between her ghost-life and justice. In the end, Ada surrenders her false identity, the town reckons with its complicity, and Mirabel finds that family isn't inherited but chosen — including an unexpected one formed with the woman whose story she told for years.
about_author: Edmund Crane is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering unsolved cases before turning to fiction. He writes from a farmhouse full of archived clippings, insisting every mystery begins with something someone refused to say out loud.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Mirabel Kavanagh records the final episode of her podcast season on the Ada Wren disappearance, revealing her meticulous archive of the town's statements. Her POV establishes obsessive order as armor against grief. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, interrupted by the arrival of two envelopes with no return address.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Mirabel opens both letters: one confesses to killing Ada Wren; the other promises 'the rest' at the anniversary dinner. Same handwriting, or nearly. Her POV; dread and exhilaration war as she realizes someone knows she'll broadcast this. Beat: the thrill of being seen curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Kept the Keys
chapters.summary: Cyrus Bell, retired deputy, listens to Mirabel's podcast from his hospice bed and recognizes his own handwriting in the confession letter — stolen from his files decades ago. His POV reveals he witnessed something in 1993 and buried it. Beat: guilt resurfacing like a body in thawing ground.

chapters.title: Thirteen Suspects, One Town
chapters.summary: Mirabel interviews townsfolk about the letters; everyone performs innocence too smoothly. She notices the diner owner flinch at Ada's name. Her POV; the town feels like a stage set after closing. Beat: creeping suspicion that everyone she grew up trusting rehearsed their alibis together.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Buried
chapters.summary: Cyrus, sensing time running out, burns part of his old case file but keeps one photograph: Ada's car at the quarry, taken hours after she vanished. His POV; tenderness toward the young people he protected wars with shame. Beat: love as an accomplice.

chapters.title: The Caterer Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Mirabel meets Delia Marsh, hired to cater the anniversary dinner, who asks unsettlingly precise questions about the case. Mirabel notes Delia's hands — a scar matching a detail never made public. Her POV. Beat: uncanny recognition she can't yet name.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Mirabel reconstructs the night of the disappearance and finds five alibis that interlock too perfectly, like fingers laced. Her POV; the podcast becomes interrogation. Beat: the horror that the truth may be a conspiracy of kindness rather than malice.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Confession, Draft One
chapters.summary: Cyrus dictates a true confession to his hospice nurse, then stops — naming names would destroy the found family he built from the town's orphans and strays. His POV. Beat: the weight of a secret kept so long it became a load-bearing wall.

chapters.title: The Quarry Photograph
chapters.summary: An anonymous package sends Mirabel the quarry photo. Timestamp analysis shows it was taken by a police camera — meaning law enforcement knew and said nothing. Her POV; fury at the institution she once trusted. Beat: betrayal reframing the entire case.

chapters.title: Delia's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Mirabel confronts Delia, who deflects with recipes and riddles but lets slip a phrase only Ada Wren used in her classroom. Mirabel leaves shaken, half-believing the impossible. Her POV. Beat: hope arriving disguised as absurdity.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Writer
chapters.summary: Handwriting analysis confirms two authors: the confession is Cyrus's stolen words; the promise letter is fresh ink. Someone alive wrote it recently. Mirabel suspects Delia. Her POV; the mystery splits in two. Beat: the hunter realizing the prey may be hunting her.

chapters.title: Cyrus Names a Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus tells Mirabel, obliquely, that Ada wasn't taken — she left, and he helped hide the why. He gives her a locker key before the morphine takes him. His POV. Beat: confession as gift, incomplete on purpose.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: In the bus station locker, Mirabel finds Ada's journal: she fled an abusive husband, the then-deputy chief, and the town chose to protect her by erasing her. Her POV; tears and rage. Beat: the victim revealed as author of her own vanishing.

chapters.title: The Deputy Chief's Toast
chapters.summary: The former deputy chief, now beloved patriarch, announces he'll speak at the anniversary dinner. Mirabel watches him charm the town and understands what Cyrus feared. Her POV. Beat: dread wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Cyrus, near the end, gathers the people he sheltered over thirty years — runaways, widows, Delia among them — and asks them to witness whatever happens at dinner. His POV. Beat: a dying man arranging his last act of protection.

chapters.title: Mirabel's Choice
chapters.summary: Mirabel must decide: expose Ada's survival and shatter the town's fragile peace, or bury the truth and betray her life's work. She drafts two episode finales. Her POV. Beat: the journalist's oath colliding with the human heart.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Delia visits Mirabel, nearly confessing, then presses a place card into her hand: seat three, next to the deputy chief. 'Ask him about the quarry.' Her POV. Beat: allies signaling in code.

chapters.title: Cyrus Rises
chapters.summary: Against medical advice, Cyrus attends the dinner in a wheelchair, carrying the unburned half of his file. His POV; terror and resolve. Beat: a man walking into the room where his silence began.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The deputy chief raises his glass to 'thirty years of healing.' Cyrus stands and confesses — not to murder, but to the cover-up. The room fractures; the chief lunges for the microphone; Delia drops her serving tray. Alternating POV. Beat: the truth detonating mid-toast.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Delia removes her apron and speaks: 'My name is Ada Wren. I'm still alive.' She recounts the abuse, the flight, the town's chosen blindness. The chief is arrested on Mirabel's recorded evidence. Multiple POV. Beat: resurrection as accusation.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Fallout: charges against Cyrus are dropped given his condition; the town grapples with having preferred a myth to a woman. Mirabel releases the final episode unedited. Her POV. Beat: grief and relief sharing a table.

chapters.title: Seat Three, Empty No More
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Cyrus dies holding Ada's hand; Mirabel eulogizes him beside the found family he built. Ada and Mirabel begin recording a new podcast — together. Her POV closes the book. Beat: memory transformed from burden into inheritance.
